attempted_claim: Let 0<s<2/3, let f∈C^3([-6,6]) satisfy ||f||_{C^3([-6,6])}≤c and inf_{[-6,6]}|f''|≥d>0, and put Γ={(x,f(x)):x∈[-1,1]}. If μ is an s-Frostman measure supported on Γ, is it true that for every ε>0, ||μ̂||_{L^6(B_R)}≲_{c,d,s,ε} R^{(2−min{3s,1+s})/6+ε} for all R≥1?
decisive_failure: No audit-grade proof or disproof of the L^6 bound was obtained. Naive decoupling gives only exponent 7(1-s)/12; dyadic coarea gives only rho^{2s/3} or rho^{3s-1} versus the needed rho^{min{3s,1+s}}; global energy analysis diverges on dimensional grounds. Computational evidence is limited to exact AP coincidence counts for N<=30 and heuristic Frostman calibration, which support sharpness but prove no upper bound. No verification-critical artifacts beyond the worklog were produced; closing the gap requires refined-decoupling machinery outside the bounded session.
